# Message List

## Concept

### Pitch

The chat history of prompt mode: the prompts sent to the harness and its responses, as a conversation.

### Shape

#### Description

Conversation-style, shows send prompts on the right, received input on the left.

#### Sent Prompt

A sent prompt shows the compiled markdown that was actually sent to the harness, rendered as markdown, once it has compiled. Its message header shows the name of the hidden anchor it was compiled from.

#### Response

A response from the harness is grouped by general type, in the order it happened. The harness's own text is shown as markdown. Tool calls in a row that share a general type (reading and searching files, editing files, running commands, the web, agents, and anything else) are gathered into one group, headed by that type and how many calls it holds. Each call in a group lists the tool's name, its most telling argument, and whether it is running, done, or failed, spelled out rather than only coloured.

#### Queue Background

The header along the top of the message list, holding the pinned prompt and the queue, has the same background colour as the tab bar.

#### Legibility

The output from a realtime agent should be readable and meaningful.  Make sure the font size is large enough, that the colours are legible.

content.text:
Both changes are done and all 72 tests pass. I haven't run the app to look at the result on screen.

**Relative paths:** any path inside the project directory in a tool call now shows relative to it: `/home/…/repl/src/main.rs` becomes `src/main.rs`, and the directory itself becomes `.` (so `cd /home/…/repl && …` reads `cd . && …`). This covers file paths, search paths and paths inside commands. A directory whose name only starts the same way, like `repl2`, is left alone. Conversations reloaded from history get this too.

**Command formatting:** there was no ready-made formatter to use. `shfmt` isn't installed, and I didn't find a good Rust library for it offline. So I wrote a small one in `src/shell_format.rs`:
- Long commands are split at `&&`, `||`, `|` and `;`, one command per line, with the chained ones indented:
  ```bash
  cd crates/app
    && cargo build --release 2>&1
    | tail -20
    || echo "failed && more";
  git status
  ```
- It leaves alone anything inside quotes, `$(…)`, parentheses or braces, and comments. Lines with a heredoc (`<<EOF`) and the heredoc's text are also kept as written.
- Commands of 60 characters or less on a single line stay as they are, so `ls | head` isn't broken up.
- Commands are now kept whole. Before, they were cut to their first line and 120 characters.
- They're shown as a bash code block with syntax colouring. That meant turning on gpui-kit's `tree-sitter-bash` feature in `Cargo.toml`, and it built offline.

It only breaks lines at those operators. A single long command with lots of flags still wraps normally rather than being split at each flag; I can add that if you want.
